samples.summary: The durability-lapse tooltip requirement is covered only by direct calls to the pure `tooltipFor`; nothing tests that a lapse published through context actually reaches the chip — and the provider nesting silently discards the durable client's reasons.
samples.evidence: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` ("the tooltip on a state that is now designed rather than inevitable") calls `tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)` directly with a hand-supplied lapse, so it passes regardless of whether `useDurabilityLapse()` ever answers anything. No test in the diff renders `SyncStatusChip` (or any consumer) beneath a `DurabilityLapseScope`: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` has only a `Probe` for `useDocumentDurability()`, never `useDurabilityLapse()`, and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` asserts nothing about lapse. That gap hides a live defect: `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:220` wraps `children` in `DurabilityLapseScope lapse={lapse}`, and those children are `CollabDocumentProvider`'s `inner`, which at `collab-document-provider.tsx:302` mounts its *own* `DurabilityLapseScope` with `lapse === undefined` whenever `decided.durable` is true. The inner provider shadows the outer, so `dropped`, `too-large`, `out-of-space` and `write-failed` can never be read by anything under the document provider — exactly the opposite of the comment at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:196 ("this wins where it has an answer"). The design requirement the tests cite ("its tooltip must name which case applies") therefore reads as covered while being unreachable in the app.

samples.summary: The "local cleanup can never fail the operation" property asserted in comments on `logout` and `deleteDocument` has no test: both `await` the cleanup with no guard of their own.
samples.evidence: auth.ts:120 states the erase is "never able to fail the sign-out itself", and documents.ts:163 states the purge is "never able to turn an accepted deletion into a reported failure", yet both sites are a bare `await` (`await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()`, `await purgeOfflineDocuments([id])`). The new suites mock those helpers: `tests/api/auth.test.ts` mocks `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` with `vi.fn(async () => {})` and never makes it reject; `src/api/documents.test.ts` mocks `purgeOfflineDocuments` and never gives it a rejecting implementation. So no test would notice if a future change let the helper throw — sign-out would then skip its success toast and redirect, and an accepted deletion would be reported to the user as a failure.
searchedFor: read tests/api/auth.test.ts 'sign-out and local data' block
grep for mockRejectedValue on eraseOfflineDataOnLogout / purgeOfflineDocuments

samples.summary: The quota-specific branch of `onWriteFailure` (`outOfSpace` → the `out-of-space` lapse) is never exercised: the only failure driven in tests is a plain `Error`.
samples.evidence: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` fires `captured[0].onWriteFailure?.(new Error('refused'))` in every failure case, which takes only the `setWritesFailing(true)` path. Nothing constructs a `DOMException('…','QuotaExceededError')`, so the `err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'QuotaExceededError'` guard and the resulting `out-of-space` wording — the one cause the design says the user can act on — are untested end to end. (The `tooltipFor` unit test supplies the `out-of-space` string by hand, which does not exercise this producer.)

samples.summary: The `keepArchives` option added to `dropAllForUser`/`eraseOfflineData` has no caller and no test, so the branch it guards is entirely unexercised.
samples.evidence: `grep keepArchives packages/frontend` returns only the two declarations (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1085/1123 and offline-erase.ts:29) and the explanatory comment; no call site passes it and no test in `offline-erase.test.ts` or `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` sets it. The prose at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1116 describes it as being "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this" (the expired-session path), but that path now erases nothing at all (`eraseLocalData: "none"`), so the option is dead and its `if (!options.keepArchives)` branch is only ever taken one way.

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser` — the regex that keeps the orphan-snapshot sweep from deleting another account's rows — has no test.
samples.evidence: `grep -n 'orphan|belongsToAnotherUser'` over `packages/frontend/src/lib/*.test.ts` finds only the change-row orphan case in `wafflebase-doc-store-robustness.test.ts:32` and the orphan-header case in `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts` ("is collected rather than living forever out of reach"), both with keys that carry no `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` segment. No case seeds a snapshot whose key names a different user and asserts it is skipped, nor one that names this user and asserts it is collected — so a regex change that matched nothing (collecting another account's orphan) or matched everything (never collecting any orphan, re-creating the permanent quota leak the sweep was added for) would pass the suite.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repo exercises the durability-lapse context path. A repo-wide grep for the token `Lapse` matches only 5 source files plus a design doc — zero test files — so nothing mounts `DurabilityLapseScope` or calls `useDurabilityLapse`. The only lapse coverage is `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632-633`, whose `stranded()` helper calls the pure `tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)` with a hand-supplied lapse; it renders nothing and passes regardless of whether the context ever delivers a value. Test files importing `@/lib/durable-document-context` use only `useDocumentDurability` (durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:61) or `DurableDocumentScope` (use-sync-status.test.ts:17, sync-status-chip.test.tsx:28) — the durability context, not the lapse one — and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` (read in full) asserts only clientKey/store/election/subscription facts. No e2e directory exists. The gap has real impact because the wiring is in fact broken: durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:209-224 publishes `dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed` around `children`, but those children are collab-document-provider.tsx:363 `{inner}`, and `inner` at :301-313 mounts its own `DurabilityLapseScope` whose lapse is `undefined` when `decided.durable` (:291-299) — shadowing the outer value, so the design requirement ("its tooltip must name which case applies") is unreachable in the app while reading as covered. Missing test over a changed, user-visible behavior; major.
